title: 2026-09-22-luminate-health-eval-scope-workshop
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC focused on quality evaluation for Luminate Health's clinical summarization use case. Agreed to define golden prompts (100 canonical cases), construct a regression suite (2.5k examples), hallucination/format checks, and a blended scoring approach (accuracy + hallucination penalty + style/format score). Benchmarks include latency and cost targets; next steps: Redwood to send evaluation spreadsheet, security pack, and proposed pilot timeline; customer to share sample dataset and success thresholds.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Really excited to dig into the eval plan for the summarization POC. Sound good on time? We have about an hour and change.
[00:12] Rachel (Head of Product): Yep that's fine. We've got Samir, Ellen and Priya here.
[00:18] Samir (ML/Infra): Hi, thanks. We're mainly trying to validate quality before we commit to dedicated infra. So the evaluation has to be very clear.
[00:28] Diego (SE): Great. Quick agenda: agree on success criteria, define golden prompt set, size the regression/holdout suites, outline hallucination checks and format validation, and touch on perf/cost targets and timeline.
[00:38] Ellen (CTO): Sounds good. We want a plan we can hand to our QA/clinical review team.
[00:44] Maya: Awesome. Rachel, could you start us off with top-level success criteria from product?
[00:50] Rachel: Sure. For the summarization flow we need three things: one, clinical accuracy — any hallucination risks are a non-starter for us; two, consistent output format that maps to our downstream parser; three, latency under 650ms p50 in our production flow, ideally.
[01:05] Maya: When you say hallucination non-starter, do you have a quantitative threshold? Like percent of hallucinations per 1000 summaries?
[01:12] Rachel: We were thinking less than 1% critical hallucinations, and overall hallucination rate under 3% across the dataset. Critical meaning anything that could change a clinical decision.
[01:23] Diego: That's very helpful. We'll capture that as a hard success gate. We typically implement a multi-tier scoring: factuality checks + structural/format checks + human-in-the-loop sampling. For the POC we can make the acceptance criteria be: factuality score > 90, hallucination rate < 3%, format compliance > 98%.
[01:40] Samir: How do you compute factuality score? Is it model-based or reference-based?
[01:45] Diego: Good question. We recommend a hybrid: exact-match checks for key fields (medication names, dosages, dates), and entailment-style LM checks for free-text statements. For POC we'll use reference-based metrics on the gold set and an entailment/regression model for broad coverage. Note that entailment models can be noisy, we'll calibrate them with human labels.
[02:02] Priya (Data Engineer): On datasets — we can share 3k redacted examples for the regression suite and 120 canonical cases we'd like flagged as golden prompts. Some of those are edge cases.
[02:14] Maya: That's perfect. Our typical ask is 100–200 golden prompts — sounds like you can provide 120 which is ideal. For the regression suite 3k is good but we should stratify by complexity.
[02:26] Rachel: Stratify how?
[02:28] Diego: By length (short note vs multi-page consult), by specialty (cardio, oncology, etc.), and by presence of tables or numeric labs. We'll want roughly 60% typical, 30% edge, 10% rare.
[02:41] Ellen: On privacy, we need to be clear: any PHI must remain in our environment. We'll use Redwood Private or dedicated with VPC. Security pack is a must.
[02:52] Maya: Understood. We'll send the Private deployment spec and SOC 2 / ISO docs. Are you leaning Private or Dedicated?
[02:59] Samir: Probably Private for the pilot unless cost pushes us to Dedicated. We need KMS/HSM support and audit logs.
[03:07] Diego: Both are supported; the main difference is control plane access and network boundaries. We'll include detailed notes on KMS and retention. Also, small note: sometimes the auto-transcript says 'kay vee cash' for KV cache, but yes we do KV cache for context reuse.
[03:23] Rachel: Back to scoring — you mentioned a hallucination penalty. How is that integrated into an overall score?
[03:29] Diego: We propose a composite score: Composite = 0.6 * factuality_score + 0.2 * format_score + 0.2 * hallucination_penalty where hallucination_penalty is 100 - (10*hallucination_rate) or a similar mapping to penalize severe hallucinations more. We can tweak weights based on your priorities.
[03:48] Samir: So for example if factuality is 92, format is 99, hallucination rate 2% -> halluc_penalty = 100 - 20 = 80. Composite = 0.6*92 + 0.2*99 + 0.2*80 = 55.2 + 19.8 + 16 = 91. So that passes a >90 threshold.
[04:06] Maya: Nice, we'll include that formula in the eval spreadsheet.
[04:09] Jordan (SE): About hallucination detection — we do lexical overlap checks for entity hallucination and an LM-based verifier for statements. We'll flag any hallucination that asserts new facts not supported by the source. We'll also do citation-matching for source-text pull-through.
[04:24] Rachel: Citation matching would be huge for clinical review. Can you output confidence + source spans?
[04:29] Diego: Yes, we can include per-field confidence and source offsets. For the POC we'll output per-token logprobs as well if you want to run your own filters. Note that exposing token-level logs has privacy considerations — but within Private it's fine.
[04:44] Priya: We'll want strong format validation because our downstream parser fails if JSON blocks are malformed. Is Redwood able to enforce schema?
[04:52] Diego: Absolutely. We'll include a strict schema checker as part of the eval: mandatory fields, enum values, and regex checks for date/dosage formats. We'll report format compliance percentage.
[05:03] Ellen: Perf targets — earlier Rachel mentioned p50 < 650ms. Can we get p99 goals?
[05:09] Maya: Common enterprise targets are p50 < 650ms, p95 < 1.2s, p99 < 2.5–3s depending on model and batch. If you use a smaller quantized model we can hit lower numbers. We'll include target bands.
[05:22] Samir: Cost sensitivity: what's the expected token cost at our expected volume? We're estimating 10 million tokens per month for the pilot traffic shape.
[05:31] Diego: We'll estimate after we get your prompt/response length distribution. For rough math, at 10M tokens we can show cost ranges for the recommended model family: open-xx-1Q (quantized variant), medium variant, and larger family. We'll include cost per 1M tokens and projected monthly. We'll also include batching and prefix cache gains — those might cut 20–40% off token consumption for repeated context.
[05:53] Rachel: Can we run a smoke benchmark on a small subset to estimate latency and token cost?
[05:58] Maya: Yes. Proposed sequence: 1) Redwood runs dry-run benchmark on 200 examples (mix of golden + typical) to collect p50/p95/p99 and cost per call; 2) run full regression of ~3k examples for quality scoring; 3) run longer stability load test for throughput. Sound good?
[06:18] Samir: Timeline for that?
[06:20] Maya: If you share data and access by Thursday, we can run the dry-run within 3 business days, full regression in 1 week, and load test following that — total POC 4–6 weeks depending on remediation cycles.
[06:32] Priya: We can aim to share the sample set by Wednesday EOD.
[06:36] Ellen: Who will be the point of contact on Redwood?
[06:38] Maya: That's me, Maya. Diego and Jordan will run the benchmarks. We'll also include an SRE contact if needed.
[06:46] Rachel: Regarding regression tests — you mentioned 2.5k vs 3k. We can commit to 3k but we want to hold out a 500-case blind set for the clinical team.
[06:55] Diego: That's fine. We'll reserve 500 for blind evaluation and 2.5k for regression and tuning. We'll also set up a golden set (the 120 canonical cases) that are evaluated every run to track regression.
[07:07] Maya: On evaluation metrics, we'll return: exact-match on structured fields, normalized-string match for names/meds, BLEU/ROUGE-ish for free-text, entailment score distribution, hallucination rate, format compliance, and latency/cost.
[07:22] Samir: Do you provide tooling to visualize these metrics?
[07:25] Jordan: Yes — Redwood Console will have per-model dashboards, per-route metrics, and the eval dashboard will show pass/fail per test, trend lines, and the ability to filter by specialty or length. We'll share screenshots.
[07:38] Rachel: For the human review loop, how do we sample?
[07:41] Diego: We recommend stratified sampling: 5% of production traffic, upweighted edge cases, and any failures from automated checks. We'll also do targeted sampling on low-confidence outputs.
[07:54] Priya: On the hallucination detection, sometimes the LM-based verifier flags benign paraphrases. How do you reduce false positives?
[08:00] Diego: We calibrate the verifier against your human labels and adjust thresholds. We'll also tune to reduce penalizing paraphrase-only deviations by focusing verifier on factual claims and named entities.
[08:13] Ellen: Security reminder — we need SSO/SAML, RBAC by team, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also retention controls for logs and token-level traces.
[08:23] Maya: We'll include SAML/SSO doc, RBAC options, and audit-log forwarding setup. Retention policies can be configured per-customer.
[08:31] Rachel: Any major blockers you foresee?
[08:34] Diego: Main technical risk is evaluation label noise for entailment checks; we'll budget for a small manual label pass (~300 examples) to calibrate. Infrastructure risk is throughput if you choose the largest family without dedicated capacity, but that's solvable with Dedicated or Private.
[08:49] Maya: Let's talk acceptance gates before we wrap. Proposed: 1) Composite score >= 90 on blind holdout; 2) Hallucination < 3% and critical hallucination < 1%; 3) Format compliance >= 98%; 4) Latency within agreed band depending on model. Agreed?
[09:06] Rachel: Agreed.
[09:08] Samir: Agreed with the caveat we'll review the composite weights after first run.
[09:12] Maya: Perfect. Last bit — logistics and next steps.
[09:15] Diego: We'll also provide a runbook for the POC including how to reproduce benchmarks and steps to escalate.
[09:22] Priya: Can you share a sample eval spreadsheet straight away?
[09:25] Maya: Yes, we'll send the spreadsheet and a template for golden prompts.
[09:29] Jordan: And we'll include instructions to run the Redwood CLI for private deployment smoke tests.
[09:35] Ellen: When can we see pricing?
[09:38] Maya: We'll include estimated token costs in the spreadsheet and a pilot quote for 6 weeks.
[09:42] Rachel: Okay, that's great.
[09:44] Maya: Cool — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs.
[09:47] Samir: Thanks.
[09:48] Ellen: Thanks all.
[09:50] Maya: End call.

Note: transcript contains ASR artifacts and occasional mis-attributions. Intentional shorthand left in to reflect Fireflies export style.
